Are AIs "Grown" or Built? Analyzing Chapter 2 of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies

Released Aug 14, 2026, 44 min

Play Are AIs "Grown" or Built? Analyzing Chapter 2 of If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies on YouTube
Watch on YouTube

Are AI models "grown" like crops, or engineered like software? And why are AI safety writers so obsessed with painting LLMs as bizarre, unpredictable alien minds?

In this video, we continue our chapter-by-chapter breakdown of "If Anyone Builds This, Everyone Dies" by analyzing Chapter 2. We put their provocative "Grown, Not Crafted" analogy to the test, untangle the messy dialectic around LLM autocomplete vs. "true understanding," and address the infamous incident where Bing Chat allegedly threatened a philosophy professor.

While there is a modest, valid point buried here—that modern deep-learning models are too complex for humans to predict in every scenario—the broader claims about AI preferences and "alien minds" are woefully under-defended and rely on subtle leaps in logic.
